reason: Implement the personal-use access loop requested by the owner without creating a commercial licensing platform. Yance gets one lightweight shared personal-access authority so the OWNER installation remains permanently usable, TESTER installations must submit an access request, the owner can move requests through ASSIGNED and APPROVE/REJECT, and approved testers can later be SUSPEND/REVOKE. Existing channel account/identity tables remain channel authorities and must not be relabeled as human product users. Existing SQLite/r32_meta is reused only for local installation/access receipts; the shared authority is a small package-specific Cloudflare Worker/D1 service with simple installation binding to discourage casual credential sharing. The access guard must fail closed for non-owner product API use when no active tester authority exists, while preserving a minimal access/status/request surface needed to obtain approval. This work package does not authorize cloud backup, billing, subscriptions, payment, anti-tamper DRM, formal release or publishing.

digestCanonicalization.pathNormalization: Require exact repository-relative normalized paths, remove duplicates, then sort with JavaScript default Array.prototype.sort().
digestCanonicalization.canonicalText: Join the normalized sorted unique path list with LF and append exactly one trailing LF before hashing.

expectedFailures: Current product has no OWNER/TESTER human access authority and therefore cannot distinguish the owner's permanent use from a tester requesting access.
Current product has no shared request lifecycle capable of PENDING/ASSIGNED/APPROVED/REJECTED and no tester grant lifecycle capable of ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/REVOKED.
Current local API security authenticates the desktop-local caller but does not enforce owner/tester product entitlement, so an unapproved copied installation is not product-access blocked.

reviewedCandidates.name: PocketBase
reviewedCandidates.reason: Mature single-binary backend with authentication, but adopting its user/auth model would create a second general-purpose identity platform and database authority when this package needs only OWNER/TESTER request, grant and installation-binding state.

reviewedCandidates.name: Supabase Auth
reviewedCandidates.reason: Mature JWT user-management service, but the required capability is not general login/token issuance; adding a general user identity authority would duplicate existing local API authentication and exceed the package-specific entitlement scope.

reviewedCandidates.name: Keycloak
reviewedCandidates.reason: Mature IAM product, but realms, federation, OIDC/SAML and general identity administration are materially broader than the two-role personal-use entitlement lifecycle and violate the explicit no-general-purpose-license-or-identity-platform constraint.

reviewedCandidates.name: Existing Yance local security seams
reviewedCandidates.source: electron/credentialVault.js + existing local API session security + SQLite/r32_meta receipt storage
reviewedCandidates.reason: These seams correctly own owner-secret storage, local caller authentication and local receipt caching, so they must be reused; they cannot alone provide shared server-authoritative tester suspension/revocation across copied installations.

retireOrAvoid: Avoid introducing Supabase/Auth0/Firebase/Keycloak/PocketBase or another general-purpose human identity platform for this package.
Avoid relabeling channel accounts, external identities, Facebook OAuth identities or messaging-route identities as OWNER/TESTER product entitlement truth.
Avoid creating a second local authentication system; preserve existing local API session security and add only the entitlement guard.
Avoid plaintext owner administration secrets in SQLite; reuse electron/credentialVault.js for the local privileged secret boundary.
Avoid hardware fingerprinting, strong DRM, billing, subscription, payment or commercial license machinery.

uncoveredGap.capability: A tiny shared, server-authoritative OWNER/TESTER request-and-grant state with simple installation binding and immediate SUSPENDED/REVOKED enforcement, while OWNER remains locally usable.
uncoveredGap.reason: No existing repository seam or reviewed mature OSS can supply only this narrow entitlement truth without either remaining local-only or introducing a broader identity/authentication platform. The authorized Cloudflare Worker + D1 code is therefore a package-specific minimal gap, not reusable general-purpose infrastructure.
rejectedAdoptionModes: full-product: Keycloak-class IAM is substantially broader than the required two-role personal entitlement loop.
sidecar-service: PocketBase/Supabase Auth introduce general user/auth database and token authorities that duplicate existing authentication.
source-module: embedding an OSS identity module still creates a second human identity/auth authority rather than the required narrow entitlement state.
official-sdk-cli-native-prebuild-runtime: SDKs can access a remote store but do not themselves provide the required server-authoritative lifecycle semantics.
existing-repository-seam: credentialVault, local API session security and SQLite receipts are reused but cannot enforce remote tester suspension/revocation across installations.
thin-yance-adapter: there is no already-owned upstream entitlement authority to adapt to without first adopting an over-broad identity product.

devicePolicy.goal: discourage casual sharing, not strong DRM

negativeProofs: A fresh unapproved installation cannot use protected product APIs and can only reach the entitlement request/status surface.
OWNER remains usable and can perform ASSIGN, APPROVE, REJECT, SUSPEND and REVOKE operations.
APPROVED creates an ACTIVE TESTER grant bound to the requesting installation; a different installation cannot silently reuse it.
SUSPENDED and REVOKED are enforced by the product guard and cannot be converted to ACTIVE by local cached state.
Worker/network failure never promotes PENDING, REJECTED, SUSPENDED or REVOKED tester state.
Channel account, external identity, Facebook OAuth and messaging route authority behavior is unchanged.
